conditions: SM clock LOCKED to 1755 MHz; drift-controlled (rotated measurement order, median of 3 rounds)

check1_2_moe_crossover_and_raggedness.root_cause: vLLM ships NO tuned bf16 config for E=8,N=14336 on H100 (only fp8_w8a8 / H200). The default heuristic uses GROUP_SIZE_M=1 below ~M=1280, which cripples L2 reuse of expert weights across M-blocks -> bf16 is anomalously slow in the T=256-512 band. This is real, deterministic vLLM behavior (reproduces to <0.1% across runs), not measurement noise.
check1_2_moe_crossover_and_raggedness.small_T_control: def/g16 = 0.995-0.997 at T<=128 (GROUP_SIZE_M irrelevant with few M-blocks) => method validated AND small-T fp8 win (1.77-1.89x) is config-INDEPENDENT/robust

crossover_tokens.reconciliation: Against a FAIR (tuned) bf16 baseline the measured crossover (263) matches the roofline (334) ~ 300 tokens. The original ~600 was INFLATED by vLLM's under-tuned stock default (GROUP_SIZE_M=1) in the T=256-512 band. The 706 anchor-interp value was a sparse-interpolation artifact and is dropped.

robust_claims: large-T fp8 loss 0.63-0.78x (T>=640) holds vs BOTH stock and tuned bf16 (worse vs tuned)
crossover ~300 tokens vs a fair baseline; ~600 vs stock out-of-the-box vLLM

check3_mla_washout_robustness.finding: FP8 KV does not merely wash out -- it LOSES monotonically at high batch (0.96x @ B=32 -> 0.71x @ B>=64), robust and stable. Root cause: the fp8 with_kvcache decode kernel saturates KV bandwidth at ~0.8 TB/s, BELOW the bf16 sparse_fwd kernel's ~1.9 TB/s, so fewer bytes/token does not translate into lower latency once batch is large.
check3_mla_washout_robustness.confound: low-batch win (3.1x) is confounded by vLLM's two-kernel dispatch (fp8->decode kernel, bf16->prefill-style sparse_fwd; the latter is inefficient at B=1). The high-batch LOSS is the robust, deployment-relevant signal.
